_comment: CloudWatch Logs metric filters and alarms deployed against the CloudTrail log group. Account ID and log group name are redacted; substitute your own before applying. Filter patterns map to the Sigma rules in ../sigma/.

metricFilters.notes: The invokedBy and eventType clauses exclude activity AWS services perform on the account's behalf, which would otherwise present as root usage.
PutEventSelectors is included because coverage can be silently narrowed without ever stopping the trail. StartLogging is excluded; see the Sigma rule for reasoning.

validation.knownGap: 5 matching events produced 1 notification - CloudWatch alarms notify on state transition, not per event. PutBucketPolicy events against the log bucket (5bfa1454, 240b1b5e) are out of scope for this filter.

metricFilters.notes: Fires on legitimate administrative activity by design. Severity is determined at triage by requestParameters.policyArn, not by the API call itself.

validation.falsePositiveNote: AttachUserPolicy with ReadOnlyAccess - legitimate administration, generated deliberately as a control case
validation.knownGap: CreateUser (80f8ece9) not matched by this filter

_designNotes.threshold: Set to 1 because these are low-frequency, high-signal events. Volume-based thresholds are inappropriate here; a single occurrence is the signal.
_designNotes.treatMissingData: notBreaching prevents the alarms from sitting in INSUFFICIENT_DATA when no matching events occur, which is the normal state.
_designNotes.period: 300 seconds matches CloudTrail's delivery characteristics. Shorter periods do not improve detection latency because delivery to CloudWatch Logs is itself the bounding factor.
_designNotes.whyCloudWatchLogsNotS3: S3 delivery lags 5-15 minutes and cannot trigger an action. CloudWatch Logs is the only path that supports alarming, which matters most for the tampering detection since StopLogging is the last event a trail will record.

_validationSummary.primaryLimitation: CloudWatch metric alarms notify on state transition rather than per event. Per-event delivery requires EventBridge rules.
